methodology: Five consecutive verses individually screened; Qur'an Arabic and Mustafa Khattab English context read on Quran.com 12:81; Genesis 42 and 44 Mechon-Mamre English primary translation directly inspected. No direct dependence asserted. Distinguish parallels from loose motifs and absent passages. Not a critical original-language or manuscript study.

assessments.subject: Brothers instructed to report Benjamin's alleged theft
assessments.evidence: Genesis records Judah offering himself instead and does not narrate a report of Benjamin's theft to Jacob.

assessments.subject: Appeal to townspeople and caravan as witnesses
assessments.evidence: Genesis 44 and 42 do not present the appeal to town and caravan witnesses.

assessments.subject: Jacob suspects the brothers and resolves on beautiful patience
assessments.evidence: Genesis has Jacob accuse his sons of bereaving him and refuse Benjamin's departure; the Qur'an places this reaction after Benjamin is detained and includes hope in God's restoration.

assessments.subject: Jacob turns away in grief for Joseph; eyes become white
assessments.relationship: loose grief motif with significant distinction
assessments.evidence: Genesis 44 records Judah describing Jacob's fear of death from grief; it does not narrate whitened eyes or Jacob turning away at this point.

assessments.subject: Sons warn Jacob that continual remembrance of Joseph will destroy him
assessments.evidence: Genesis 44:30-31 expresses fear for Jacob's life but does not report the sons directly reproaching him for remembering Joseph.

dossier.title: Jacob's grief and his sons' report after Benjamin's detention
dossier.comparative_summary: Qur'an 12:81–85 presents the report to Jacob, appeal to witnesses, Jacob's mistrust and beautiful patience, grief for Joseph and his sons' admonition. Genesis 42:36–38 depicts Jacob's earlier distress and Genesis 44:27–34 describes his grief prospectively through Judah's speech, but Genesis 44 ends before any return/report to Jacob. No whitened eyes, caravan witness appeal or equivalent admonition occurs in these inspected passages.

dossier.chronological_background: Genesis belongs to pre-Islamic Jewish scripture. Literary composition, textual redaction, translation histories and extant manuscript witnesses are different chronological questions; no specific date established in this batch.
dossier.scholarly_interpretations: Shared Joseph narrative tradition and Qur'anic theological reframing are comparative hypotheses, not proof of direct borrowing.
